report:
Reviewed the complete meta.book.chapter_names claim and all two implementation/four test entries. Baseline verification: exact joined-line comparison against the supplied historical input confirms spec.rs and spec_plan.rs are byte-identical. The only test-source delta replaces review inventory claim access with a fragment selector in a different test; all three associated ordinary test bodies and the TODO body remain unchanged. Historical rationale was reassessed against current sources, not treated as execution evidence.

Source assessment: spec.rs chapter_namespace strips design/, accepts .md and .sage, removes the README terminal component, normalizes hyphens to underscores, validates each component as an ASCII identifier, and joins components with dots. qualified/add_chapter_text attach the local definition name; this gives the claim's meta.anchors.point_excerpts example and preserves fully qualified Rust-reference spelling. Naming has no heading/title inputs; load_workspace collects destination paths in a set so sidebar labels/order cannot enter names. It diagnoses colliding normalized namespaces, duplicate qualified anchors and output URLs. Its Sage prose path passes the same chapter namespace to add_chapter_text; full Sage integration remains deferred by explicit evidence below. The Rust reference examples describe the qualified name, not a separate Rust parser guarantee.

The complete ordinary test set supplies visible meaningful assertions: canonical_inventory_uses_configured_chapters_and_local_names asserts the exact meta.authority/meta.call_rules.declared names, README namespace and context URL using a real configured book; chapter_namespace_collisions_and_duplicate_local_rules_are_errors asserts normalized-path collision and duplicate full-name diagnostics plus rejection of dotted components and paths outside Design; distinct_namespaces_cannot_publish_the_same_output_url asserts README/index publication ambiguity. A regression omitting qualification, normalization or collision diagnostics would fail these assertions. Captured BookFixture setup/write/load confirms they exercise SpecIndex::load_workspace with real files, not an opaque assertion helper.

The ordinary spec implementation association is supported by these behaviors. The spec_plan.rs TODO implementation and todo::names_derive_from_chapter_paths test explicitly defer the complete .md/.sage naming and display-title/sidebar-order invariance scenarios. The empty body proves nothing and remains TODO. Its prerequisite is replacing the planned stub with fixtures comparing qualified names across Markdown and owned Sage chapters, collision cases, and heading/title/sidebar changes; existing Markdown coverage is partial progress, not completion of that integration matrix. No N/A entries exist. This retains the historical justified deferral without claiming implemented or tested completeness for the pending scenarios.

Execution: personally ran review start with coordinator instructions, review read for BookFixture and review policy, and exact baseline comparison/source inspections. No behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer; the coordinator's reported 321 passing sage-meta tests and root build are separate baseline execution evidence. No source changes or requested edits.
